text:
casey: node alert from customer-123: prolonged 504s, p95 sky-rocketed around 12:02 UTC. saw a ton of inflight requests hitting the hosted gateway. can someone look? :rotating_light:

eng-oncall-bot: [ALERT] hosted-gateway queue depth > 950 for pool=prod-hosted-eu, tail-504s detected, triggered notification at 1903204300.

jordan: i'm seeing continuous-batcher lag on the metrics dashboard — queueing time percentiles jumped from 10ms to 1.2s around 12:01.

maria: logs from the gateway show repeated 5xx upstream with "request handler timeout" and "batcher-schedule-delay". copying a snippet:```
[12:02:05] gateway: route=/v1/generate tenant=customer-123 req_id=abcd1234 status=504 msg="handler timeout" queue_depth=972 batcher_delay_ms=1234
[12:02:07] batcher: evicting early req_id=efgh5678 reason=queue_limit
```

ryan: customer claims traffic spike but rate seemed normal from their side (~120rps). could be many small concurrent requests that blow up batching.

casey: can we repro locally? steps to try: 1) run many concurrent short prompts to /v1/generate with tenant header, 2) force continuous batching to target small seq_len, 3) set gateway max-queue to 1024 and watch.

jordan: i spun up a repro harness (script attached). quick diff: when concurrency > 800 with our default batcher concurrency, queue depth climbs and the scheduler starts dropping/evicting tails, generating 504s. snippet:```bash
# quick repro
for i in {1..1000}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer TEST" -H "X-Tenant: customer-123" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":8}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
done
wait
```

maria: noticed config anomaly: the hosted gateway had a recent override to reduce max_worker_threads on the batcher pool (PR #3124) — that reduces throughput under high-concurrency, increases queueing risk.

support-ops: customer is on a production plan and seeing impact on user experience. they've opened a support ticket; asking for ETA and temporary mitigations.

jordan: mitigation options: 1) temporarily raise gateway queue cap (fast but increases memory/latency), 2) enable early-fallback to smaller model to reduce per-request tokens, 3) throttle tenant at edge (rate-limit per-tenant), 4) adjust batcher concurrency to allow more inflight batches.

casey: immediate plan: i'll raise max_queue to 1600 for prod-hosted-eu and revert the PR that reduced worker threads. doing a staged change and monitoring p95. also enabling tenant throttling at 150rps as soft-limit.

eng-oncall-bot: [ACTION] change applied: gateway.max_queue(prod-hosted-eu)=1600 by casey at 1903204402.

maria: rolling back PR #3124 on the batcher pool now. should restore previous worker_threads=24. started at 1903204420.

ryan: after changes, observed queue depth drop to ~120 and p95 back to ~90ms. no new 504s in last 3m.

support-ops: relaying update to customer. they asked for root cause analysis and permanent fix suggestions.

casey: followups (action items): - create a tenant-level circuit-breaker that rejects with 429 before queueing when token/concurrency thresholds exceeded (owner: jordan) - add a golden config test to block low worker_threads in prod (owner: maria) - instrument batcher evictions metric to alert earlier (owner: ryan)

jordan: added GH issues and assigned. also will prototype a progressive-fallback that switches to lower-cost model when queueing > 50th percentile for 30s.

maria: logging note for postmortem: correlate batcher_delay_ms and queue_depth with model type and sequence length to find optimal per-tenant cap.

casey: closing on immediate incident — will file a short postmortem and coordinate with support for customer compensation if needed. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
